Class OrderRepository

java.lang.Object
com.andreibel.server.dbController.repository.OrderRepository
public class OrderRepository extends Object
JDBC repository for Order persistence and retrieval.

This repository encapsulates all SQL access to the bistro.Order table using plain JDBC. It relies on TransactionManager for obtaining the current transactional Connection via TransactionManager.currentConnection().

Transaction requirement: all methods are expected to run inside an active transaction (for example via tx.inTransaction(...)). Calling these methods without a transaction may result in null connections or unexpected behavior.

Order lifecycle flags: the repository uses soft state flags rather than deleting rows: orderCancelled, orderArrive, and orderCompleted. Some methods update these flags (e.g., arrival, cancellation, completion) and scheduler-related methods perform batch updates based on time conditions.

Implemented as a thread-unsafe singleton (sufficient for typical single-instance server usage). If you use multiple class loaders or need concurrency-safe lazy init, adjust getInstance().

Author:
Andrei Beloziyorove

    • findAllSubscribersOrders

      public List<Order> findAllSubscribersOrders() throws SQLException
      Loads all orders that belong to a subscriber (i.e., subscriberId IS NOT NULL).

      This method is useful for subscriber history/report screens. If you want truly "all orders", remove the subscriberId IS NOT NULL filter.

      Returns:
      list of subscriber orders (possibly empty)
      Throws:
      SQLException - if a database access error occurs

    • findActiveOrders

      public List<Order> findActiveOrders() throws SQLException
      Loads all currently active orders (arrived but not yet completed or cancelled).

      An order is considered active when:

      • orderArrive = 1 (customer has checked in)
      • orderCompleted = 0 (not yet closed)
      • orderCancelled = 0 (not cancelled)
      Returns:
      list of active orders (possibly empty)
      Throws:
      SQLException - if a database access error occurs

      public List<Order> findOrdersCollideByDateTime(LocalDateTime date) throws SQLException

      Only active orders are considered: not cancelled and not completed. This method is typically used during availability checks in order creation logic.

      Returns:

    • save

      public Order save(Order newOrder) throws SQLException
      Persists a new Order row and returns the stored entity reloaded from the database.

      Nullable fields (subscriberId, email, phoneNumber) are inserted as SQL NULL when missing. After insertion, the method reads the generated primary key and calls findById(int) to return a fully mapped object.

      Parameters:
      newOrder - order to persist
      Returns:
      stored order (reloaded by generated key)
      Throws:
      SQLException - if insert fails or no generated key is returned

    • deleteByConformationCode

      public int deleteByConformationCode(UUID conformationCode) throws SQLException
      Soft-cancels an order by confirmation code.

      The row is not removed from the database. This method sets orderCancelled = 1 and returns the number of affected rows (typically 0 or 1).

      Parameters:
      conformationCode - order confirmation code
      Returns:
      number of updated rows
      Throws:
      SQLException - if a database access error occurs

    • findAllDateOrders

      public List<Order> findAllDateOrders(LocalDate date) throws SQLException
      Loads all not-cancelled orders that start within the given calendar date.

      The filter uses a half-open interval: [date 00:00, (date+1) 00:00). Only orders with orderCancelled = 0 are returned.

      Parameters:
      date - day to fetch (local date)
      Returns:
      list of orders for the given day (possibly empty)
      Throws:
      SQLException - if a database access error occurs

    • cancelLateOrders

      public List<Order> cancelLateOrders(int graceMinutes) throws SQLException
      Batch-cancels late orders (no arrival within a grace period).

      An order is considered late if it is not cancelled, not completed, not arrived, and its orderDateTime is earlier than now - graceMinutes. The method updates rows by setting orderCancelled = 1.

      Parameters:
      graceMinutes - allowed lateness window in minutes (e.g., 10–20)
      Returns:
      list of orders that were cancelled (for printing notifications)
      Throws:
      SQLException - if a database access error occurs

    • findOrdersDueToClose

      public List<Order> findOrdersDueToClose(LocalDateTime now) throws SQLException
      Batch-completes arrived orders that should be closed now (fixed 2-hour duration).

      This method is intended for a scheduler. It marks orders as completed when: they are not cancelled, arrived, and their orderDateTime is earlier than now - 2 hours.

      Parameters:
      now - reference time used to compute the cutoff now.minusHours(2)
      Returns:
      list of orders that were closed (for printing invoices)
      Throws:
      SQLException - if a database access error occurs

    • getCountInThisMount

      public Map<LocalDate, Integer> getCountInThisMount() throws SQLException
      Counts subscriber orders per day for the current month.

      Only orders with a non-null subscriberId are counted. Results are grouped by date and returned as a map.

      Returns:
      map of date to subscriber order count for the current month
      Throws:
      SQLException - if a database access error occurs

    • getCountInThisMonthByTime

      public Map<LocalDate, Map<LocalTime, Integer>> getCountInThisMonthByTime() throws SQLException
      Counts arrived orders per day and time slot for the current month.

      Only orders with a recorded arrival time (orderArriveDateTime IS NOT NULL) are included. Results are grouped by date and time, useful for generating customer traffic reports.

      Returns:
      nested map of date to (time to order count) for the current month
      Throws:
      SQLException - if a database access error occurs

    • getLateOrders

      public Map<LocalDate, Integer> getLateOrders() throws SQLException
      Counts late arrivals per day for the current month.

      An order is considered late when the customer arrived after the scheduled reservation time (orderArriveDateTime > orderDateTime). Results are grouped by date for reporting purposes.

      Returns:
      map of date to late order count for the current month
      Throws:
      SQLException - if a database access error occurs
